paper.abstract_en: Cosmologically relevant minisuperspaces are shown to be equivalent to dynamical systems defined by a simple Hamiltonian akin to the standard form <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e61"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">H</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">∼</mo><msup><mrow><mi>η</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msup><msub><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">q</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, where the symplectic structure on phase space is not the canonical one. The associated quantum frameworks are constructed via geometric quantization, leading to a Wheeler–DeWitt equation which exactly matches the one of the associated standard quantum cosmology models. This imparts a purely symplectic interpretation to the classical and quantum cosmological dynamics. Some noncommutative generalizations are also constructed.
